basic_info.title: L2MM: Learning to Map Matching with Deep Models for Low-Quality GPS Trajectory Data
basic_info.venue: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data (TKDD), Vol. 17, Issue 3, Article 39 (February 2023; DOI registered 2022)

method.critic_note: graph_integration downgraded to [uncertain] by critic-anti-drift: agent set GNN_road_embedding but its own summary described L2MM as RNN/seq2seq representation learning with no GNN mentioned. Verify before asserting.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: L2MM learns trajectory/path representations in a latent space (with two enhancement schemes: high-frequency-trajectory enhancement and data-distribution regularization) and maps low-quality GPS to paths via a seq2seq-style joint optimization, but it relies on an RNN/seq2seq encoder rather than a transformer over a vectorized semantic road graph, it makes no sequential RL decisions, and it is trained with supervised path/trajectory pairs and high-quality reference trajectories rather than label-free on raw fleet GPS. It carries no RDF/KG semantic enrichment.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Directly targets aligning noisy, low-sampling-rate GPS to the road network, which is the central preprocessing problem for BMW fleet-trajectory analytics, though it offers no semantic-graph or label-free latent-RL component.
